title: Workflow Intake Analysis Demo
subtitle: A practical Python and SQL workflow for turning inconsistent synthetic intake into validated, traceable results.
why_built: I built this project to show how I approach inconsistent operational data: define the business rules, preserve uncertainty, separate records that are ready for use from those that require review, and produce results that can be traced back to their source.

I wanted the project to show that I can translate an ambiguous business problem into clear requirements, validation logic, SQL-backed analysis, tested technical outputs, and documentation that both technical and business stakeholders can use.
lead_problem: Inconsistent intake data can create false confidence. An unknown value may be silently converted into an affirmative fact, while records that still require context may be mixed into the same dataset as records that are ready for reporting.
human_judgment: One issue that stood out to me was how an unknown boolean value was handled. Converting an unclear value to true may make the record easier to process, but it also invents a fact that was not present in the source. I decided that the uncertainty needed to remain visible and the record should be routed for review instead.
design_decisions: Separate valid records from review-required records so questionable input remains visible without weakening the meaning of the valid dataset.
Preserve raw values alongside normalized values so each transformation remains explainable and traceable.
ai_use: I used AI-assisted tools to help brainstorm edge cases, draft and refactor parts of the implementation, suggest tests, and audit the code and documentation for consistency. I directed the project, defined the goals and business rules, reviewed the proposed changes and test results, checked the generated outputs, and made the final decisions. I treated AI output as working material rather than evidence; the technical claims are supported by reproducible code, schemas, SQL, automated tests, and reconciled results.
limitations: This project uses synthetic data and runs locally. It was designed as a professional-quality demonstration rather than a live production deployment. It does not claim live integrations, production authentication, enterprise-scale operations, or measured business outcomes. Human review remains necessary when a record requires context that the available data does not provide.
lesson: A workflow becomes more trustworthy when uncertainty stays visible and every reported result can be traced back to its source and rule.
next_improvement: I would add configurable rule profiles, reviewer dispositions, and testing over larger synthetic batches before developing a separate production-oriented version.
